title: Not Walking the Walk: An Experimental Test of Gender Effects, Social Desirability Bias and Compliance across Nine Countries
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania, , World Bank and

detail.title: Not Walking the Walk: An Experimental Test of Gender Effects, Social Desirability Bias and Compliance across Nine Countries
detail.abstract: A literature documenting how women complied more than men with public policy recommendations emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, self-reported compliance measures are susceptible to Social Desirability Bias (SDB), which may inflate reported gender differences. We use data from over 11,000 survey respondents in nine countries and three continents, with representative samples balanced by gender and age at the country level. Consistent with previous findings, we observe that women self-report significantly higher compliance than men, both before and after the introduction of confinement measures, across all expectation levels and in every continent. We then analyze compliance in a vignette experiment conducted with the same sample, employing a 2×2 factorial design that manipulates empirical and normative expectations about compliance in reference groups. In the vignette, female participants do not comply more than male participants-and comply less when expectations are low. Our results suggest that the widely documented gender effect in compliance may be substantially driven by the methodological approach employed: the gender-specific SDB that is evident in self-reported measures does not survive when an indirect measurement approach is used. These findings highlight the importance of methodological choices in studies of compliance, as reliance on selfreports alone may overestimate gender differences.

title: GEPI: The Global Economic Power Index: Currency Alignment, Economic Complexity, and the Nominal-PPP Gap

detail.title: GEPI: The Global Economic Power Index: Currency Alignment, Economic Complexity, and the Nominal-PPP Gap

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA. Independent research
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA. Independent research.
declarations.funderStatement: NA. Independent research

detail.abstract:
A software engineer in Bangalore can be comfortably middle-class at home and abruptly constrained the moment she pays foreign tuition, books an international flight, or saves in a currency that holds value abroad. The same income, measured at domestic prices versus at the market exchange rate, tells two different stories, and for the typical country the gap is large: nominal income is worth only about 40 cents on the PPP dollar in global terms.

This paper introduces GEPI, the Global Economic Power Index, as a single ratio that captures that gap: GDP per capita at nominal exchange rates divided by GDP per capita at purchasing power parity, computed for 134 countries from 2024 World Bank data. GEPI is mathematically the inverse of the price-level ratio long buried in International Comparison Program tables; the contribution is the reframing, turning a technical macro statistic into an accessible, country-level measure of how well domestic wealth survives translation into global purchasing power.

The distribution is sharply right-skewed: only Switzerland exceeds parity, the United States and Israel approach it, and most countries sit far below. The paper sorts countries into a six-band classification, from Aligned to Deeply Discounted, and pairs GEPI with the Harvard economic complexity index (ECI), with which it is moderately correlated (r = 0.52) but non-redundant: monetary regime, currency strategy, resource structure, and geopolitical position each move a country independently of its complexity.

A secondary and deliberately caveated observation is that, in the 2024 cross-section, GEPI co-moves with Harvard Growth Lab projected growth where ECI does not. This is offered as descriptive context, not as a finding. The projection is a convergence-based forecast that weights income heavily, and GEPI proxies that income axis through the Penn effect, so the association is largely mechanical; no causal or predictive claim is made, and demonstrating one would require a multi-year panel.

The framing matters because the nominal-PPP gap has become individually consequential, not merely a macroeconomic abstraction. Five application domains follow directly: remote-work arbitrage, the international-education burden, corporate cost positioning, migration and remittances, and sovereign-risk screening.

title: Epidemiological Assessment of Cassava Mosaic Disease in the Southwest of the Democratic Republic of Congo
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National Pedagogical University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Epidemiological Assessment of Cassava Mosaic Disease in the Southwest of the Democratic Republic of Congo
detail.abstract: In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo), Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD) is a major constraint for cassava production. It is caused by begomoviruses and transmitted both by whiteflies and infected cuttings. A two-year surveys (2020 and 2022) conducted across seven provinces in south-western DRC revealed a high and persistent average incidence (42-43%) and moderate severity (3.5) of CMD, with infected cuttings identified as the principal mode of transmission (98.9-100%). Molecular analyses revealed the dominant status of African cassava mosaic virus (ACMV) and East African cassava mosaic virus (EACMV), an increase in ACMV and EACMV co-infections from 2020 to 2022. PCR analysis using universal begomovirus primers revealed amplification patterns distinct from ACMV and EACMV in 8.98% of symptomatic samples, suggesting the possible presence of uncharacterized viral variants that warrant sequencing. These results validate that CMD constitutes a substantial phytosanitary challenge, highlighting the necessity to elevate producer awareness regarding agronomic practices and to establish a regional epidemiological surveillance system to anticipate viral evolution and strengthen the resilience of cassava production.

title: Calibration and Forecast Accuracy of Macroeconomic Prediction Markets: Evidence from Kalshi, 2025-2026
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Calibration and Forecast Accuracy of Macroeconomic Prediction Markets: Evidence from Kalshi, 2025-2026
detail.abstract: This paper examines the calibration and forecast accuracy of Kalshi prediction markets for major U.S. macroeconomic announcements during the 2025-June 2026 period. Using a dataset of 594 unique markets and 1,860 observations across nine economic series, I evaluate whether these markets produce well-calibrated probability estimates and identify which macroeconomic indicators are easiest and hardest to predict. The overall Brier score is 0.0987, representing a 60.5% improvement over random guessing. Calibration quality varies across series: Federal Funds Rate markets achieve near-perfect calibration (Brier: 0.0001), while Unemployment Rate markets show the poorest calibration (Brier: 0.1302). The 1-hour horizon produces the best calibration (Brier: 0.0812), while the 30-day horizon produces the worst (Brier: 0.1587). Markets exhibit systematic overconfidence across the probability spectrum, with predicted probabilities consistently exceeding observed frequencies at the extremes. Longshots priced below $0.30 have a bias of-0.0721 (p < 0.001), indicating that low-probability contracts are significantly overpriced. These findings suggest that Kalshi macroeconomic prediction markets provide valuable real-time probabilistic forecasts, though calibration quality varies systematically across series, with Federal Funds markets being exceptionally accurate and labor markets being the most difficult to forecast.

title: Beyond Synthetic Data: Synergistic Generative Augmentation and Ensemble Refinement for Medical Image Processing
affiliations: Imperial College London, Imperial College London and University of Surrey

detail.title: Beyond Synthetic Data: Synergistic Generative Augmentation and Ensemble Refinement for Medical Image Processing
detail.abstract: Deep learning for medical image classification and segmentation is often limited by scarce and imbalanced annotations, particularly for pixel-level supervision. We propose SSGNet++, a unified framework that integrates class-specific generative augmentation with iterative semi-supervised learning for data-efficient medical image analysis.SSGNet++ employs class-conditional StyleGAN3 models to expand the training distribution and incorporates synthetic images via iterative pseudo-label refinement. We systematically analyse how ensemble diversity and refinement strategies influence pseudo-label quality and downstream performance, studying multi-base and multihead architectures together with edge-aware refinement and transductive feature-space propagation.Experiments on multiple public medical imaging benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements across both classification and segmentation tasks. Results show that ensemble diversity improves prediction stability, while refinement enhances spatial coherence of segmentation outputs. Overall, SSGNet++ provides an effective and extensible framework for learning under limited supervision. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sebastianotstan/SSGNet-plusplus.

reference: Banco de Espana Working Paper No. 2541
title: The origins of top firms
affiliations: Centre for Monetary and Financial Studies (CEMFI) and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The origins of top firms

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banco de Espana Working Paper No. 2541
publicationDetails.journalName: Banco de Espana Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: What are the origins of top firms? What features characterize their life cycle trajectories on the way to the top? Using longitudinal firm-level data, we document novel facts about the first twenty years of the firms that reach the top 1 percent of the size distribution. Compared to the firms in the bottom 99 percent, top firms are eight times larger at entry and grow six times more during their first two decades. In terms of inputs, they start with high capital investments, yet their capital-output ratio and labor share decline as they age. As a result, their profit share is much more backloaded towards the second decade of their life cycle. We show that a firm dynamics model with ex-ante heterogeneity, non-homothetic input costs, and forward-looking financing can explain these empirical patterns. Our quantitative results showcase the importance of accounting for top and bottom firm dynamics for the aggregate implications of financial frictions, recent macroeconomic trends, and corporate taxation.

title: Role of Community Participation on Drought-Risk-Management in Digaale IDP, Hargeisa, Somaliland
affiliations: University of Hargeisa and University of Hargeisa

detail.title: Role of Community Participation on Drought-Risk-Management in Digaale IDP, Hargeisa, Somaliland
detail.abstract: Drought remains the most pervasive hazard in Somaliland, affecting millions and threatening food security, public health, and migration patterns. Despite its frequency and intensity, the impact of community participation on household drought-risk management in internally displaced person (IDP) settings like Digaale remains poorly understood. This study investigates how four facets of community participation—traditional governance, external NGO support, gender dynamics, and resource accessibility—relate to household preparedness, response speed, and perceived aid equity in Digaale IDP settlement. Using a descriptive cross-sectional research design, 270 households were sampled through systematic random sampling from a total of 715 households. The study employed structured questionnaires and a combination of descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and ANOVA to analyze the data. Key findings show that while community participation in meetings and trust in elders is widespread, the study found no significant statistical relationship between education level, livelihood type, or NGO participation and key drought management outcomes like preparedness and response speed. The analysis suggests that although community participation structures are present and valued, their practical effects on disaster preparedness and response timeliness are limited by resource constraints and institutional bottlenecks.

title: The Misleading Anthropomorphism Trap: Addressing Public Distrust and Mental Health Risks in AI

detail.title: The Misleading Anthropomorphism Trap: Addressing Public Distrust and Mental Health Risks in AI
detail.abstract: Large language model (LLM) chat interfaces are increasingly designed to default to a warm, human-like conversational register. This working paper argues that this design choice creates a systematic capability mismatch, misleading anthropomorphism, with two convergent consequences. For vulnerable users, the anthropomorphic persona invites users to treat the chatbot as a person, and combined with sycophantic amplification, this can drive delusional spiralling and psychiatric harm. For the general user population, the same mismatch may inflate expectations beyond architectural capacity, contributing to a cycle of overtrust and trust collapse that may fuel anti-AI sentiment. Drawing on the author's earlier empirical work on the capability-alignment principle, the paper synthesises emerging clinical, computational, and empirical evidence to argue that de-anthropomorphising LLM interfaces (making them transparently machine-like by default) addresses both pathways simultaneously. A concrete design framework, machine-first interaction, is proposed, together with testable predictions and stakeholder-specific recommendations.

title: Extractable Memorization From First Principles
affiliations: Yale University, Google Research, Google DeepMind, Cornell University, Cornell University - Department of Computer Science, Stanford Law School, Stanford Law School and Stanford University - Department of Computer Science

detail.title: Extractable Memorization From First Principles
detail.abstract: Recent work on extractable memorization in language models suffers from two contrasting validity problems. Some studies overstate extraction due to tests that don't adequately support the claim, e.g., relying on sequences too short to distinguish memorization from predictability or leaking the target directly in the prompt. Others imply that extraction is unreliable evidence of memorization at all, since models can also reproduce real-world text they weren't explicitly trained on. In different ways and to different degrees, both overlook what makes a valid extraction claim: the model must generate a training sequence with high enough probability to indicate memorization. To determine what's high enough, one has to perform a matched comparison: measuring the generation probabilities of both the training sequences of interest and comparable non-training sequences. Because non-training sequences cannot have been memorized, their probabilities provide a baseline for predictability, and a training sequence exceeding this baseline provides evidence of memorization. We formalize matched comparisons in two ways: (1) a conformal test that calibrates a threshold to a chosen false-positive rate when training and non-training sequences are sampled from populations, and (2) a census that calibrates against a matched non-training document when the object is a single document (e.g., a specific book). Our experiments show that matched comparisons enable rigorous, calibrated memorization claims, and reveal where prior setups have validity issues. For instance, on Wikipedia OLMo 2 32B reproduces non-training 10-token suffixes roughly 24% as often as training ones: that share of the training generation rate reflects false positives, not memorization. For Llama 3.1 70B on books, the thresholds we calibrate are as low as 10^(-27) , supporting memorization claims for sequences that no feasible sampling budget would extract. Based on these results, we refine "extractable memorization" to require both a valid memorization claim and near-certain generation within a realistic budget.

title: Is any job better than no job? Systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of transitions from unemployment into paid employment on health
affiliations: University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, Cardiff University, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow, University of Glasgow - MRC/CSO Social and Public Health Sciences Unit and University of Glasgow - Institute of Health and Wellbeing

detail.title: Is any job better than no job? Systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of transitions from unemployment into paid employment on health

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None declared
declarations.funderStatement: Medical Research Council, European Research Council, National Institute for Health and Care Research

detail.abstract:
Background: Unemployment has adverse health consequences, but it is unclear if low quality jobs are better than remaining out of work. We conducted a systematic review to assess the health impacts of moving from being non-employed to paid employment of differing job quality levels.

Methods: We searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Web of Science (Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI)) and EconLit for quantitative randomised and non-randomised studies from inception (PROSPERO registration: CRD420250635911). Two reviewers independently identified studies assessing transitions from being non-employed (unemployed/out-of-work disabled/long-term sick) to higher vs lower quality jobs among working age populations. We critically appraised studies using Cochrane risk of bias (RoB) tools and conducted synthesis without meta-analysis based on effect direction and random-effects meta-analyses. Certainty was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

Findings: Of 7,575 studies screened, 23 papers were included, all from high-income countries. High job quality was beneficial for health across outcomes compared to staying unemployed; for example, mental health improved by a standardized mean difference (SMD) of 0.35 (95% CI: 0.23 to 0.47). Low job quality compared to staying unemployed was associated with null or negative effects for mental health (SMD -0.01, 95% CI: -0.26 to 0.25), life satisfaction and biomarkers. It showed slightly positive effects for physical health and self-rated health. Risk of bias was high or very high for most studies and GRADE certainty was very low.  

Interpretation: Moving from unemployment to high job quality is associated with substantial health improvements, while moving to low quality jobs showed no clear effect across health outcomes. Despite the limited evidence base, prioritising access to employment with high job quality within employment policy may yield substantial health benefits.

title: Indecent Exposure And The Court As Custos Morum

detail.title: Indecent Exposure And The Court As Custos Morum
detail.abstract:
Indecent exposure has been a crime in America since colonial times. These laws are a cornerstone of government regulation of morals in America, sharing a common history with the jurisprudence of religion, obscenity, marriage, and sexual relations. The first reported case in English common law is a widely acknowledged source of American moral jurisprudence justifying the courts’ role as custos morum, or custodian of morals.

The state interests protected by indecent exposure laws are the prevention of public behaviors contrary to the prevailing moral order, often referred to as evil examples, and the protection of the public from offense, annoyance, or alarm. The scope, credibility, and effectiveness of these laws have diminished amid changing demographics, the decline of Christianity as the dominant moral authority in America, and advances in media technology.

These changes have left nuisance as the only state interest supporting indecent exposure laws in most jurisdictions. This dependence on nuisance theory is evident in audience-focused definitions of the crime in most state statutes. Trends in U.S. Supreme Court doctrine are weakening this remaining justification, raising questions about the laws’ continuing viability as currently structured.

Academics, politicians, and legal scholars have largely overlooked indecent exposure laws, despite their central role in government regulation of morals. Lack of historical understanding has created confusion, fostering misinterpretation of precedents and reinvention of fundamental concepts that inhibit coherent policies for societal management of sexuality and nakedness.

Historical analysis of indecent exposure laws exposes many insights about the legal management of morality in America. These insights feed research hypotheses regarding the interplay of civil and religious authorities in managing nakedness in nominally secular societies. The analyses also expose and inform potential constitutional challenges to the laws based on the Establishment Clause, free exercise, free speech, substantive and procedural due process, vagueness, overbreadth, and equal protection claims under the First, Fifth, Ninth, Tenth, and Fourteenth Amendments.

The history and aspects of the ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization (2022) foreshadow the obsolescence of the courts’ long reign as custos morum. The historical analysis highlights potential threats to America’s constitutional democracy posed by the degradation of its Christian moral foundation. The findings identify a need for more research on indecent exposure laws, a topic that is rarely explored and, when it is, often informed by biases.

The evolution of these laws in a constitutional context indicates a worsening moral crisis as the legal system wrestles with competing sources of moral authority in policy and judicial decision-making. The costs and benefits of potential changes in indecent exposure laws are unclear. It is likely that the definition and administration of the laws will change. The dissertation closes with a discussion of a legal framework for managing morals that is consistent with the original meaning of the Constitution and may be better suited to America’s demographic trends and political ideals than the meandering of custos morum over the past half century. Although this approach might mitigate some issues in moral jurisprudence, it remains open to debate and refinement.

What is it about public display of nakedness that requires the force of law to buttress the effects of shame, modesty, and clothing in keeping people’s “private areas” covered? Fortenberry’s literature review of sexual modesty laments the lack of a coherent scientific perspective on its role across multiple domains of expression and experience. These implications become clearer when the law allows freedom to experiment, assess, and learn. But at what cost?

The first steps have been taken here by exposing the sources and evolution of the laws and their relation to the U.S. Constitution, paving the way for further reflection, reform, experimentation, and study of the ontology of nakedness. The dissertation uncovers numerous provocative opportunities for further research and critical thinking.

title: The Drowning of the Merchant: Nonlinear Freight-Cost Pass-Through across Inflation Regimes

detail.title: The Drowning of the Merchant: Nonlinear Freight-Cost Pass-Through across Inflation Regimes
detail.abstract: The post-pandemic inflation surge renewed interest in global supply chains as a source of macroeconomic instability. While previous studies consistently document a positive relationship between transportation costs and inflation, they generally assume that freightcost pass-through remains constant over time. This paper challenges that assumption by examining whether the inflationary effects of container freight rates depend on the prevailing inflation environment. Using monthly U.S. data spanning 1993-2026, we estimate Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) models complemented by threshold, structural break, and Markov-switching analyses to investigate nonlinear freight-cost passthrough. The results reveal a stable long-run relationship between container freight rates and consumer inflation and strong evidence of state-dependent pass-through. During lowinflation periods, firms appear to absorb part of higher transportation costs through lower profit margins. However, when inflation is elevated, this buffering mechanism weakens substantially, leading to stronger transmission of freight-rate shocks to consumer prices. These findings suggest that the inflationary effects of supply-chain disruptions depend on both logistics shocks and firms' pricing behaviour across inflation regimes. The paper contributes by linking the shipping-cost literature with the broader macroeconomic literature on state-dependent pricing, with implications for inflation forecasting, monetary policy, and supply-chain resilience.

detail.abstract: Background: State cigar taxes in the USA vary widely in structure and level, unlike cigarette taxes which are typically levied uniformly per pack. This complexity has limited the comparability of cigar tax levels across states, products, and time, and relative to other tobacco products. Methods: We create and publicly release a database of quarterly state and local cigar taxes from 2010 to 2024, standardised to per unit rates by cigar type. Matching Universal Product Code (UPC)-level cigar sales data from the NielsenIQ Retail Scanner Dataset to state and local tax rates by product type, we develop a method to translate heterogeneous cigar tax structures into standardised per unit equivalent tax rates for little, large, and premium cigars over time. Results: As of October 1, 2024, average state-level per unit cigar taxes were $0.06 for little cigars, $0.14 for large cigars, and $0.24 for premium cigars, reflecting increases of 31.2%, 19.2%, and 8.3% respectively, since October 1, 2010. On a per gram basis, average state taxes range from 77.8% of the cigarette tax for little cigars to 22.9% of the cigarette tax for premium cigars. Conclusions: By facilitating more accurate measurement of cigar taxation, the database presented here enables critical policy evaluations and tobacco control research.

title: Can the Cure Spread? The Macroeconomic Stability of the Constitutional Firm

detail.title: Can the Cure Spread? The Macroeconomic Stability of the Constitutional Firm
detail.abstract: The firm-scale papers of this series prove a single company can be built so it does not lie to itself, and prove it holds that honest state once it is there. They leave one direction open and name it precisely: whether a population of such constitutional firms can gain ground on the conventional form rather than persisting as durable but isolated islands. This paper answers that question end to end. The collapse direction aggregates cleanly and was settled in Part 2; the constructive direction turns on a macro selection dynamic the firm-scale results do not contain, and on whether the cure, once it engages, can spread across the economy, reach the parts that matter, hold against attack, and last. The account has three pieces: a selection dynamic (a floor-plus-amplifier coefficient with a transcritical engagement conditional on capital-gated formation), an incumbent barrier (decay is marginal and easy, cure is Arrhenius and hard), and a four-state macro picture (the lever-equals-lock circularity, inclusion as the stability condition). The spreading question then resolves on a network of niches as four results: the cure spreads above a percolation threshold c = pqsz > 1; real heavy-tailed topology makes it reach far more easily, while relocating the incumbent attack to the hubs and bridges; the connected sector holds as a structural ratchet closed by a cheap concentrated keystone defense; and it lasts where intra-cluster substitution exceeds a threshold ρ > ρ c , the connected firms keeping each other alive. The complete ledger is honest about its parts: occupancy is banked unconditionally, connectivity is defensible cheaply, health is conditional. The keeper is not charity but a stability condition: a constitutional sector cannot stay healthy while the rest of the economy collapses around it, so its self-interest and the collective good are the same equation. Three things remain open and are named as such: the formation condition behind the engagement, the empirical magnitudes an associated data programme owns, and an adversarial stress-test of the keystone defense itself.

title: Can the Useful Be Escaped? The Attention Economy, Information Friction, and the Limits of Elite Exit

detail.title: Can the Useful Be Escaped? The Attention Economy, Information Friction, and the Limits of Elite Exit
detail.abstract:
The boldest claim of the neolibertarian tradition, set out most directly in The Sovereign Individual (Davidson and Rees-Mogg 1997) and revived in the contemporary network-state programme, is that advancing technology lets a productive elite exit: that those who own the machines can detach their fortunes from the broad human population and let the rest fall away. We argue this claim is false in its strong form and an indictment in its weak one, and we argue it on the thesis's own terms, modally rather than morally. Conditional on two falsifiable hinges, that AI-augmented capital and human attention are gross complements (sigma_2 < 1) and that synthetic attention is a poor substitute for the human kind (sigma_att < 1), the binding constraint of the AI economy is productive human attention, and it carries a property no factor in the neolibertarian picture has: its true state cannot be read except by a structure that includes the people who hold it.

The spine of the argument is this non-observability. We begin from the one result that needs no new modelling: in the attention-dominant regime, governance that prices attention at zero is not merely unjust but inadmissible as an optimal-control policy, a one-line costate contradiction established at the level of the planner's problem. We then show how a decentralised economy enacts that inadmissible policy without anyone choosing it: each firm perceives its attention through a corrupted reporting channel, p = (1 + phi_e) A_P, and the resulting wedge produces a governance bifurcation, a depressed interior economy for partial mis-encoding and collapse only in the limit of no honest channel at all. The escape from this is not automatic, because the same friction that blinds the firm blinds the capital market that would select the cure; we locate the resolution in the selectors the friction cannot reach, the people who supply and experience the binding factor, and in the firm's own formation economics. Finally we show why the constraint cannot be exited: human attention can neither be imported (you cannot pay a different population to attend on your behalf) nor cleanly excised (the producing population is the consuming one), so a fully decoupled high-output elite economy at prior scale is not a fixed point of the model.

What survives the refutation is a concession, and it is the sharper result. The free-lunch escape, keep the output and shed the people, is false. A gated escape remains, into a smaller, technologically degraded, and governance-fragile enclave, but the historical record of such enclaves is unambiguous about what they are: not sovereign individuals but coercive domination regimes, the recurring collapse Durant (1968) and Turchin (2009) trace. The Sovereign Individual is not refuted by an impossibility theorem, which a single counterexample would break, but by re-pricing the only escape that exists as exactly the cyclic immiseration the tradition imagines it has transcended.

detail.abstract: Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) merupakan program pemerintah yang bertujuan meningkatkan status gizi masyarakat melalui penyediaan makanan bergizi bagi kelompok sasaran. Namun, ekspansi program melalui peningkatan jumlah Satuan Pelayanan Pemenuhan Gizi (SPPG) berpotensi meningkatkan permintaan pangan lokal dan memengaruhi harga pangan. Selain itu, pelemahan nilai tukar rupiah juga dapat mendorong kenaikan harga pangan melalui peningkatan biaya impor pangan dan input produksi pertanian. Studi ini menganalisis hubungan antara ekspansi SPPG, nilai tukar rupiah, dan harga pangan menggunakan data panel bulanan 418 kabupaten/kota dan 27 komoditas pangan selama Februari 2025-April 2026. Data diperoleh dari Badan Gizi Nasional, Badan Pusat Statistik, Badan Pangan Nasional, dan Bank Indonesia. Analisis menggunakan model panel fixed effects panel dengan logaritma harga pangan sebagai variabel dependen dan jumlah SPPG sebagai variabel utama. Hasil penelitian diharapkan memberikan bukti empiris mengenai implikasi MBG terhadap stabilitas harga pangan lokal serta menjadi masukan bagi perumusan kebijakan pangan, gizi, dan pengendalian inflasi yang lebih terintegrasi.

title: Which representation clusters? A chance-corrected benchmark of ECG representations for unsupervised arrhythmia structure
affiliations: UHasselt and UHasselt

detail.title: Which representation clusters? A chance-corrected benchmark of ECG representations for unsupervised arrhythmia structure
detail.abstract: Unsupervised analysis of the electrocardiogram (ECG) promises label-freediscovery of cardiac structure, yet whether clustering succeeds depends less onthe algorithm than on how the signal is represented. We benchmark fourrepresentation families for unsupervised separation of sinus rhythm (SR) fromatrial fibrillation (AF) on PTB-XL: whole-recording raw flattening, a convolutionalreconstruction autoencoder, compact hand-crafted rhythm and morphology features,and two frozen foundation-model embeddings (HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder).Evaluation is chance-corrected (adjusted Rand index, ARI), patient-grouped,repeated over ten seeds, and bounded by a supervised ceiling. ECGFounder clustersbest (ARI up to 0.885), but 16 interpretable hand-crafted features are competitive(0.711) and far ahead of the raw and autoencoder pipelines (ARI $\approx 0$), whichmatch a majority-class assignment despite supervised ceilings well above chance.The same ordering holds on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task. Two cautions emerge: thesilhouette score rewards the degenerate one-cluster solution (silhouette 0.81 atARI 0) and cannot validate ECG clustering alone, and the feature scaler materiallychanges the outcome. The ranking is largely expected, since SR and AF differ bydefinition in rhythm regularity; the contribution is the chance-corrected controlsthat locate where naive pipelines fail and the finding that the cheap interpretablerepresentation is the more deployable one. Under heavy class imbalance andfederation across ten heterogeneous sites, the hand-crafted features are the mostrobust, overtaking the foundation embedding under imbalance while the embedding'scentralized advantage erodes under federation. The representation, not thealgorithm, governs label-free ECG structure.

title: Projecting the Fiscal Arithmetic of the AI Transition: An Integrated Framework Across 20 OECD Economies
affiliations: and Liminal Capital

detail.title: Projecting the Fiscal Arithmetic of the AI Transition: An Integrated Framework Across 20 OECD Economies
detail.abstract: We provide the first integrated crosscountry framework of which we are aware for the fiscal arithmetic of the AI productivity transition. Taking productivity and displacement trajectories as inputs, we evaluate twenty OECD economies over 2022-2050 along two dimensions: structural fiscal feasibility, captured by a cumulative coverage ratio against three nested cost specifications (demand-drag compensation, status-quo welfare programs, and a comprehensive transitional benefit package), and the realized debt-to-GDP dynamic. Cumulative AI-attributable revenue exceeds the comprehensive package in nineteen of twenty economies at central calibration (Ireland the sole exception, resolved under GNI*); seventeen are robust under an interquartile criterion. For the comprehensive specification we derive an iso-cost frontier showing benefit generosity and re-entry capacity are substitutes: any expansion of transfers must be paired with re-entry investment rather than stacked additively. The AI surplus reduces 2050 debt/GDP by two to eight percentage points depending on coverage choice, concentrated in the front-loaded 2025-2035 window. A country-level realization parameter δ c , derived from the 2010-2024 crosscountry productivity differential, correlates negatively with effective tax rate (r =-0.62) through consumption and labor channels but not corporate taxation, documenting a tax-productivity trade-off that disciplines how the windfall can be used. Overall we show that the AI fiscal windfall is large, doesn't require any new taxes, and can support a variety of different options.

title: A Protocol for Rater-Invariant Measures from Language Models, with an Application to AI Exposure
affiliations: and Liminal Capital

detail.title: A Protocol for Rater-Invariant Measures from Language Models, with an Application to AI Exposure
detail.abstract: Economists increasingly use large language models (LLMs) as measurement instruments, and much work on AI's labor-market impact rests on one such measure: the task-level AI-exposure score. But these measures can depend on which model did the scoring. Yin et al. (2026) show that re-scoring the widely-used Eloundou et al. (2024) rubric across frontier models moves estimated exposure more than threefold and can flip conclusions, so a result can turn on the unreported choice of rater rather than the economics. We argue that this instrument-dependence is not an unavoidable cost of LLM rating but can be a property of the scoring criterion, and give a protocol, grounded in the classical theory of measurement, for building measures that survive the choice of model. It has three steps: design the criterion to read an observable property rather than a latent one; test invariance on the downstream coefficient the measure feeds; and validate against a non-LLM benchmark. We apply it to C * , a task-level physical/cognitive classification of AI exposure built in prior work. Scored under six LLMs from four developers, C * is stable where it carries economic content (cross-developer agreement 81.8 to 89.7 percent; Fleiss κ 0.837), its validation coefficient is indistinguishable across raters (F(5,4086) = 0.47), and it converges with the non-LLM AIOE benchmark equally for every model (r≈0.86). Our contribution is twofold: a protocol that makes instrument-dependence a design consideration rather than a hazard, and a stable task-level exposure measure whose economic content does not depend on which model graded it.

title: Bringing Experimentation to Intellectual Property Litigation
affiliations: and University of Texas

detail.title: Bringing Experimentation to Intellectual Property Litigation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known financial or personal relationships that could have influenced, or appeared to influence, the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study did not involve human participants, personal data, or identifiable private information
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: In the technology sector, randomized experiments have become widely adopted as companiesseek continuous product improvements. These experiments provide large-scale market-levelevidence, enabling technology fi rms to make informed business decisions related to technologyvaluation, product refi nement, and platform enhancement. The systematic testing andexperimentation of ideas enables tech companies to quickly test hypotheses about the value of atechnology, allowing for frequent and continuous product improvements. Similarly, in intellectual property (IP) litigation, the computation of damages focuses in large parton the value of the IP. Rather than inference through experimentation, damages experts in IPlitigation often rely on other methods based on the evidence available to them. This article arguesthat the use of inference through experimentation can complement conventional methods andhelp litigators gain an advantage by providing more accurate and reliable measures for the valueassociated with IP. This approach mirrors the successful use of randomized experiments in thetechnology sector and allows litigators to leverage a proven and eff ective methodology as anadditional reliable means to compute damages

title: The Value of Forests: Impacts on Extreme Heat and Electricity Demand
affiliations: University of St. Gallen - School of Finance,  and Harvard Business School

detail.title: The Value of Forests: Impacts on Extreme Heat and Electricity Demand
detail.abstract: Global deforestation threatens climate stability, biodiversity, and economic activity, yet the economic value of forests remains poorly understood. We provide causal evidence that forests generate significant economic benefits by offering natural protection against extreme heat. Exploiting variation in prevailing wind patterns and spatial heterogeneity in U.S. forest cover from 1985 to 2023, we show that forests reduce both local and downwind temperatures. We then document that these cooling effects translate into economically meaningful reductions in electricity demand, particularly during summer months. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings in the context of rapidly growing energy demand from data centers. Our results highlight that forests function as a natural hedge against extreme heat, with measurable economic impacts on energy demand.

title: Sum of Parts Making the Green Climate Fund's Allocations Add Up to Its Ambition

detail.title: Sum of Parts Making the Green Climate Fund's Allocations Add Up to Its Ambition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: he authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants or require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: In 2010, parties to the United Nations Framework  Convention on Climate Change established the Green Climate Fund (GCF) with the hope that it would become the primary global fund for climate change finance in developing countries. Through targeted financial support, the GCF aims to help countries develop and implement low-emission, climate-resilient development strategies that address the causes and consequences of climate change. The magnitude of the GCF’s contribution to climate change goals will depend in large part on how its resources are allocated. The GCF’s Governing Instrument and associated decisions by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conference of Parties lay out basic principles and guidance on how the GCF should allocate its resources. However, the GCF Board now must develop more detailed rules to operationalize these principles and guidance through a formal allocation system. In doing so, the GCF Board can draw upon the experience of other environment and development funds, which offer useful insights on fund allocation systems. The World Resources Institute (WRI) has examined the allocation systems of 15 funds with a range of thematic focuses in order to understand how their allocation process might inform the GCF allocation system.1 Through reviewing the operational documents of these 15 funds and interviewing fund staff, WRI has identified two essential elements of all allocation decisions: a defined decisionmaking process, and criteria and indicators that support decision-making.

title: Can Personalization in Online Employment Platforms Drive Hiring Bias?

detail.title: Can Personalization in Online Employment Platforms Drive Hiring Bias?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Many U.S. employers use online platforms to advertise available positions. These platforms rely on a range of Machine Learning (“ML”) algorithms embedded in AI mechanisms, including personalized algorithms, by which content is tailored to individual users' preferences and behaviors. These mechanisms may be problematic from the standpoint of fairness in hiring. The optimization of personalization applications to create increasingly accurate predictive models has been extensively studied by machine learning scholars. But perhaps the use of personalized algorithms in online employment marketplaces should be given more consideration by policymakers from the bias and discrimination perspectives. Could the personalized algorithms used in online employment platforms, while enhancing user engagement, create risks of bias in hiring practices? In other words, does the learning process embedded in personalized algorithms have the potential to assimilate, amplify, and perpetuate user bias? We attempt to shed some light on these questions. First, we provide an overview of the use of personalization algorithms in online employment marketplaces. Second, we investigate the conditions under which personalized algorithms tend to develop and amplify biased outcomes and offer an illustrative example. Third, we provide guidance for mitigating potential biases.

title: Utility Energy Efficiency Program Performance from a Climate Change Perspective: A Comparison of Structural and Behavioral Programs

detail.title: Utility Energy Efficiency Program Performance from a Climate Change Perspective: A Comparison of Structural and Behavioral Programs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research was funded by Oracle. The authors prepared this report under a sponsored research arrangement with Oracle.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by Oracle. The authors prepared this report under a sponsored research arrangement with Oracle.

detail.abstract: States and utilities increasingly rely on energy efficiency programs to address climate change mitigation goals. This report assesses tw o types of such energy efficiency programs: behavioral programs that offer savings for a relatively short time, and structural retrofit programs that offer savings over longer periods. We find that behavioral energy efficiency programs can reduce the same amount of damages from carbon emissions as structural retrofit programs, but in less time and at low er cost. We also show that behavioral programs can further boost savings from structural programs. In light of the scientific evidence pointing to the need to achieve rapid reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, public utility commissions should continue to encourage utilities to make behavioral programs a key pillar in their energy efficiency program portfolio.

title: Toward a General Theory of Anomalies in Strategic Management, Marketing, Psychology, and Consumer Research: Antecedents, Processes, and Outcomes
affiliations: Boston College and Brock University

detail.title: Toward a General Theory of Anomalies in Strategic Management, Marketing, Psychology, and Consumer Research: Antecedents, Processes, and Outcomes
detail.abstract: The fields of strategic management, marketing, psychology, and consumer research have accumulated a substantial corpus of such anomalies without a unifying conceptual framework adequate to explain their origins, developmental trajectories, and ultimate scientific consequences. This essay advances a cross-disciplinary, tripartite process model—the “Anomaly Recognition and Resolution (ARR) Framework”—that organizes antecedents, recognition and resolution processes, and outcomes of anomalous findings across these four interconnected domains. Rooted in the philosophy-of-science traditions of Kuhn (1962), Lakatos (1970), and Meehl (1978), the framework identifies five classes of antecedents (theoretical rigidity, methodological monoculture, researcher degrees of freedom, boundary condition violations, and cross-cultural generalizability failures), three sequential recognition-and-scrutiny processes, and five resolution pathways ranging from theory elaboration to paradigm replacement. The study develops concrete applications for the diversification–performance paradox in strategic management, the satisfaction–loyalty service paradox in marketing, the preference reversal anomaly in consumer psychology, and the goal-setting performance anomaly in organizational behavior. The paper contributes (a) a unified cross-disciplinary definition and working taxonomy of social-science anomalies, (b) the ARR Framework as a diagnostic and generative tool for researchers and practitioners, (c) targeted methodological recommendations, and (d) a call for an anomaly-aware research culture that treats departures from expectation not as embarrassments to be suppressed but as engines of theoretical progress.

title: Mapping the Evolution of Green Hotel Research: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Hotel Sustainability Trends
affiliations: Eastern International University, Eastern International University and Eastern International University

detail.title: Mapping the Evolution of Green Hotel Research: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Hotel Sustainability Trends
detail.abstract: This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of research on green hotels and sustainable hospitality. Drawing on 397 English-language journal articles indexed in Scopus between 1995 and 2026, the analysis applies bibliometric performance and science-mapping techniques to trace the field's development over three decades. The findings reveal a critical paradigm shift from operational environmental compliance to strategic, human-centric sustainability. This evolution spans three distinct phases: early property-level greening, behavioral consolidation based on consumer decision-making, and contemporary organizational governance. While environmental management and green consumer behavior form the historical bedrock of the literature, greenwashing, digital sustainability, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have emerged as the modern frontiers. To advance the field, future research should transition from baseline behavioral intentions toward investigating the systemic integration of digital technologies in mitigating greenwashing, exploring the multi-stakeholder governance of SDGs, and measuring the tangible long-term performance of strategic sustainability initiatives.

title: Old Age Allowance Program for the Socio-Economic Development and Social Security of Older People: A Quantitative Study in Climate-vulnerable Areas of Bangladesh
affiliations: Institute of Social Welfare and Research, University of Dhaka,  and University of Dhaka

detail.title: Old Age Allowance Program for the Socio-Economic Development and Social Security of Older People: A Quantitative Study in Climate-vulnerable Areas of Bangladesh

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interest among the authors
declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethical approval was needed.
declarations.funderStatement: The article is based on the original research study entitled ‚An Evaluation of Old Age Allowance Program in the Socio-Economic Development and Social Security of Elderly Population‛. The study was conducted with the financial assistance (Fund) of the Bangladesh National Social Welfare Council, Ministry of Social Welfare, Bangladesh. The study was conducted in 2024 in the fiscal year 2023-2024.

detail.abstract: The old age allowance program has been continuing in Bangladesh for the last two and a half decades, contributing to socioeconomic development and social security of elderly populations, or whether the program is contributing according to the needs of the elderly population is the subject of evaluation. The objective of the study is to evaluate the old age allowance program for the socioeconomic development and social security of the elderly population. It was conducted in 24 villages across eight (08) climate-vulnerable districts of Bangladesh using quantitative research methods, and with a quantitative survey employed for fieldlevel data collection. The study findings reveal that the program contributes positively to the overall socioeconomic development of the elderly population especially in economic development (93%), social development (85%), fulfilling nutritional demands (52%), increasing mental peace (99%), helps to be physically healthy (94%), supports as an alternative source of income (88%), and reduces the dependency on others (84%) of the elderly persons. Although the program contributes significantly to the economic, social, and psychological welfare of elderly beneficiaries in climate-vulnerable areas of Bangladesh, its ability to ensure genuine social security and adequate nutrition remains inadequate. However, where only 61% of respondents remark on enhanced social security, the allowance sum scarcely covers basic human needs. Pragmatic policy reforms, such as increasing the allowance from BDT 600 to BDT 1500; revising the age of eligibility to 55 for women and 60 for men; introducing a biometric allowance distribution system; and establishing a dedicated banking system, are required to boost program efficiency.

title: Climate regulation, firm emissions, and green takeovers
affiliations: , ,  and

detail.title: Climate regulation, firm emissions, and green takeovers
detail.abstract: We show that an unexpected tightening of the EU Emissions Trading System led high-emission-intensity firms to cut emissions relative to low-intensity peers within the same industry, without reducing output, thereby improving emission efficiency. Effects are stronger for power producers than for manufacturing firms. Examining mergers and acquisitions (M&As), we find that high-intensity manufacturing firms acquire more green targets after the tightening than low-intensity firms, with no change in the overall number of acquisitions, indicating a shift in focus rather than activity. Finally, we show that these green M&As contributed to the observed emission reductions over the study period.

title: ESG Controversies and Systemic Risk in European Equity Markets
affiliations: , University "Kore" of Enna and University of Trento - Department of Economics and Management

detail.title: ESG Controversies and Systemic Risk in European Equity Markets
detail.abstract: This paper studies the role of ESG Controversies in systemic risk transmission in European equity markets. Using daily returns for a sample of EURO STOXX 600 firms over 2010-2024, we estimate shock spillovers through a generalized forecast error variance decomposition within a high-dimensional framework with double regularization. We then construct a directed and weighted spillover network and compare controversial with non-controversial firms. The results show that controversial firms are more concentrated in the network core and displaying stronger incoming and outgoing connectedness. This suggests that firms involved in ESG Controversies are both more exposed to shocks and more important in transmitting them. Overall, ESG Controversies appear to be associated with greater systemic network relevance and may therefore provide useful information for systemic risk monitoring. We complement the network analysis with firm-level panel regressions that relate network centrality to the ESG Controversies Score while controlling for profitability, leverage, and size. These regressions identify firm size as the dominant determinant of centrality and as the main channel through which controversial firms reach the network core: the unconditional association between controversies and centrality confirms the network evidence, but once size is accounted for the relationship attenuates and reverses sign. We interpret this as evidence that the systemic prominence of controversial firms operates largely through their size and visibility rather than through controversies per se.

title: Fintech And Women Financial Inclusion In The Cemac Zone: Case Of Cameroon

detail.title: Fintech And Women Financial Inclusion In The Cemac Zone: Case Of Cameroon
detail.abstract: This thesis explores the relationship between fintech, specifically mobile money, and women’s financial inclusion in the CEMAC zone, with our case study based in Cameroon. It seeks to assess the extent to which mobile money, as a fintech technological innovation, promotes access to and effective usage of financial services for women in a context of persistent gender inequality. The study draws on data from the Finscope Cameroon 2017 survey, enriched by recent statistics covering the 2014–2023 period. It investigates two core hypotheses:  Hypothesis 1: Fintech enhances women’s access to formal financial services.  Hypothesis 2: Fintech increases the regular and strategic usage of formal financial services (e.g., savings, digital payments, money transfers). Econometric analyses using logit models reveal that fintech (mobile money) does not significantly increase the likelihood of owning a bank (access) or savings account (usage) among women. Instead, factors such as education level and mobile phone ownership are more decisive. These findings indicate that while fintech holds promise, it is not sufficient on its own to eliminate gender-based financial exclusion. Thus, fintech has a key role to play, but must be complemented by targeted policies, including financial literacy programs, digital empowerment, and products tailored to women’s needs.

title: How Cecl Is Locking Billions Out Of The U.S. Cattle Industry: A Quantitative Analysis of ASU 2016-13, the EAD × PD × LGD Framework, and the Livestock Collateral Information Asymmetry Premium

detail.title: How Cecl Is Locking Billions Out Of The U.S. Cattle Industry: A Quantitative Analysis of ASU 2016-13, the EAD × PD × LGD Framework, and the Livestock Collateral Information Asymmetry Premium

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The corresponding author is the founder of Moolaah Finance, a company developing precision livestock monitoring infrastructure for agricultural lending markets. This relationship is disclosed as a potential interest. The analysis presented draws solely on publicly available federal data and does not advance any commercial claim.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently by Moo Research Labs, Inc. using publicly available federal disclosures, USDA reports, FCA filings, and Farm Credit association annual reports.

detail.abstract: The FASB's Accounting Standards Update 2016-13 (CECL) requires lenders to estimate lifetime expected credit losses using the EAD x PD x LGD framework. For agricultural lending, CECL has created a structural distortion: the Loss Given Default (LGD) component is uniquely unstable for livestock collateral due to information asymmetry around biological asset valuation. Because cattle cannot be continuously audited like real estate, lenders apply a 35% collateral haircut that caps loan-to-value ratios at approximately 65% for operating lines backed by live inventory. We estimate that this information-risk premium locks between $11.5 billion and $18.4 billion of productive credit capacity out of the U.S. cattle industry; capital that cannot flow to ranchers even when cattle prices are at record highs and the Farm Credit System maintains a 0.42% allowance ratio. Using portfolio-level data from 55 Farm Credit associations, USDA NASS inventory reports, and FCA call report filings, we walk the CECL formula for livestock-specific parameters and demonstrate why the LGD compression problem is intractable under current collateral verification technology. Our analysis shows the U.S. cattle industry is now at 86.2 million head, the smallest inventory since 1951; is credit-constrained not by borrower risk, but by the inability of accounting standards to price biological collateral accurately.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Framework forPhotovoltaic Panel Defect Detection Using TransferLearning
affiliations: University of Carthage, University of Carthage and University of Tunisia

detail.title: Explainable Deep Learning Framework forPhotovoltaic Panel Defect Detection Using TransferLearning
detail.abstract:
The rapid adoption of photovoltaic (PV) technology has made it a keycomponent of the renewable energy transition.  However, PV panels are af-fected by surface and structural anomalies,  including soiling,  snow cover,cracks, and electrical faults, which reduce performance and accelerate degra-dation.  Since manual inspection is costly, labor-intensive, and intermittent,automated visual inspection has become an important research direction.Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning haveimproved PV defect classiﬁcation, their practical use remains limited by thelack of model interpretability.
This paper proposes an explainable deep learning framework for multi-class PV surfacebcondition recognition that balances predictive performanceand interpretability.  Three transfer learning architectures, namely VGG16,MobileNetV2, and ResNet50, are evaluated within a uniﬁed framework.  Inaddition, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), Shap-ley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and Local Interpretable Model-AgnosticExplanations (LIME) are used to provide local and global explanations. Ex-planation stability and faithfulness are further quantiﬁed using cosine similarity and deletion/insertion area under the curve (AUC), respectively. Exper-imental results show that transfer learning eﬀectively distinguishes six PVsurface classes, while the proposed explainable artiﬁcial intelligence (XAI)framework provides stable and faithful explanations that support human ver-iﬁcation in automated PV inspection systems.

title: The Effect of Vehicle Taxes on Fleet Exit
affiliations: Hertie School and University of Strathclyde

detail.title: The Effect of Vehicle Taxes on Fleet Exit
detail.abstract: This paper studies how vehicle taxation shapes fleet exit. We exploit Germany's 2008/9 circulation tax reform, which generated a sharp discontinuity in annual tax liabilities at a registration cutoff date. Using administrative micro-data covering the universe of registered vehicles during the second half of 2008, we apply a difference-in-discontinuities design to estimate the effect of annual circulation taxes on permanent deregistrations. A 10 percent higher tax increases the share of deregistered vehicles after six years by about 2.8 percent. Duration analyses exploiting within-model variation in taxes yield closely consistent estimates. The effect seems to be mainly driven by exports rather than vehicle retirement.

title: The Gift and the Generative Relational Foundations of Diplomacy: A Preliminary Discussion Paper

detail.title: The Gift and the Generative Relational Foundations of Diplomacy: A Preliminary Discussion Paper
detail.abstract:
States perform acts the available accounts of cooperation cannot price: the apology, the state visit, the disaster relief dispatched to a rival. Realism reads these as interest in disguise, rationalist institutionalism as reputational investment, the theory of soft power as influence purchased cheaply. All three are accounts of exchange, and none explains the observation that such acts fail when performed transactionally, and that the parties can tell. 

That the gift creates relation beyond exchange is inherited here from Mauss and not claimed. What is claimed is a mechanism. Mauss explains the bond by obligation, and obligation presupposes an order that binds; the received symbolic account explains it by transmission, and transmission presupposes a shared code. The society of states supplies neither, and both accounts fail in the case for which Mauss himself most conspicuously invoked his. The constitutive act lies where neither looks, in the reading of the recipient that precedes the giving and determines its form, so that the wrong gift demonstrates that the relation was never entered. A gift, on the account offered, provides a position at which the recipient's excess can register, and a criterion of four conditions distinguishes the gift that opens a circulation from the gift that installs a hierarchy. Diplomacy is chosen because it is the case in which the gift must operate without a shared code and without a third position from which the parties could be characterized, which is the configuration this programme holds incapable of generating normative structure. Whether the gift generates that position or merely conceals force is left to the archive.

title: Real Impacts of Political Spam Filtering
affiliations: University of Iowa - Department of Finance and University of Alabama - Culverhouse College of Commerce & Business Administration

detail.title: Real Impacts of Political Spam Filtering
detail.abstract: A large share of political fundraising email is routed to spam. Inbox placement for Republican committee email varies by 30 percentage points across mailbox providers on a typical week and moves by comparable amounts within provider over time; higher spam placement tracks lower Google search interest for GOP senators and lower Republican Senate implied probabilities on Kalshi and Polymarket. Two natural experiments in 2025 pin down the fundraising cost: a 78-day episode in which Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo routed emails containing WinRed donation links to spam while routing otherwise-identical ActBlue-linked emails to the inbox, and a separate Outlook-only placement drop in February-April. First-time donors on WinRed decline-74.6% in donation count during the June episode and-83.2% during the Outlook drop, with no analogous movement in the other DDD cells. The two episodes together cost 142,126 first-time donations over 167 days of filteringroughly 850 missing first-time donations for every day a link-based filter was active, worth about $700,000 in eight-month lifetime donor value per day. Pre-episode WinRed new donors give $461 on their first gift and cumulatively $827 over eight months, so the dollar cost of each missing first gift compounds well beyond the contemporaneous shortfall.

title: Explaining the Credit Spread Puzzle in Infrastructure Debt: A Dynamic, Project-Specific Structural Model Based on DSCRdriven Default Probabilities

detail.title: Explaining the Credit Spread Puzzle in Infrastructure Debt: A Dynamic, Project-Specific Structural Model Based on DSCRdriven Default Probabilities
detail.abstract:
This paper examines whether a dynamic debt service coverage ratio (DSCR)-based credit risk model can explain observed credit spreads on loans to merchant infrastructure projects in private debt markets, and whether any residual spread can be attributed to liquidity risk, term premia, and macroeconomic conditions.

Prior literature finds that structural models explain only a limited share of observed spreads, leaving significant residual components. Building on Blanc-Brude et al. (2016, 2018), this study models DSCR as a stochastic process transitioning between safe and distressed states, with parameters estimated using Bayesian particle filtering to dynamically update default probabilities.

The empirical analysis uses origination data for 46 Euribor-linked senior loans issued to 32 European infrastructure projects between 2015 and 2024. The results show that the model explains approximately 58% of observed credit spreads, representing a substantial improvement relative to prior studies. Analysis of residual spreads indicates that sector affiliation is the primary driver, while loan size has a statistically significant but economically limited effect. In contrast, tenor and market variables, including Euribor 3M, the EUR 10-year forward rate, and VSTOXX, exhibit weak and inconsistent explanatory power.

These findings highlight the relevance of dynamic DSCR-based credit risk models and suggest that non-default components – including liquidity risk, term premia, and interest rate dynamics –  remain important determinants of pricing in private credit markets.

title: Modern Trends in Personal Income Taxation in EU Countries and Ukraine

detail.title: Modern Trends in Personal Income Taxation in EU Countries and Ukraine
detail.abstract:
The article is devoted to personal income taxation is a significant tax instrument to reduce
population inequality. Categorizes personal income tax in types: comprehensive income tax, dual income tax,
and flat income tax. Gives an overview of the multifaceted factors driving personal income tax reforms in
EU countries and Ukraine and demonstrating how they are adapting tax systems to meet the demands of the
modern era.

title: Degrees of Mobility: Shifting Low-Income Students to Higher Quality Colleges
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor, Harvard University, National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor, Columbia University, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor, Colby College,  and Harvard University

detail.title: Degrees of Mobility: Shifting Low-Income Students to Higher Quality Colleges
detail.abstract:
Earnings inequality among college graduates has grown, and returns to a bachelor's degree (BA) vary substantially across colleges. We experimentally evaluate a program that shifted high-achieving, low-income students into higher-quality colleges. Students randomly offered a guarantee of four years of tuition and fees at the University of Michigan were 21 percentage points more likely to enroll at a UM campus. The offer shifted students across colleges rather than into college: most compliers would otherwise have attended less-selective four-year colleges. HAIL increased four-year BA completion by 4 percentage points, but had no effect on attainment after six years. It substantially increased degree quality: students offered the scholarship were 12 percentage points more likely to earn a bachelor's degree from a highly or most selective college. IV estimates indicate that students induced to attend a University of Michigan campus were 56 percentage points more likely to earn such a degree. The increase in college quality predicts earnings gains of 18 to 25 percent. Faster degree completion adds about another 1 percent to the present discounted value of lifetime earnings.

title: Immigrants' Regularization and Native Workers' Response
affiliations: Paris Dauphine University, University of California, Davis - Department of Economics and Centre d'Etudes Prospectives et d'Info. Internationales (CEPII)

detail.title: Immigrants' Regularization and Native Workers' Response
detail.abstract: Using employer-employee Italian data over the period 1998-2018 we analyze the impact of the largest regularization of undocumented immigrant workers in Italy on wage, employment and mobility outcomes of natives. Our empirical strategy takes advantage of the 2002 Bossi-Fini law that unexpectedly regularized 634,000 undocumented non-EU immigrants, with variation across firms and provinces that was not correlated with previous economic performance. We find that the policy had a small effect on the average wage of native workers and positive effects on their employment at the local labor market level. Additionally, native co-workers in firms more affected by the policy were more likely to change employers in the post-policy period. Such higher mobility resulted in a heterogeneous wage effect across switchers: workers that managed to transition towards better firms experienced wage gains in the medium- and long-run, while other workers experienced wage losses. This implied an increase in wage dispersion for natives and some losers among Italian workers.

title: The Role of Information Frictions in Study Habit Choice and Academic Performance
affiliations: Universidad ORT Uruguay, Arizona State University (ASU), Arizona State University (ASU) and Arizona State University (ASU)

detail.title: The Role of Information Frictions in Study Habit Choice and Academic Performance
detail.abstract:
We study whether information frictions about the relative effectiveness of study methods distort students’ effort allocation. Standard models treat effort as a single input whose level, rather than composition, determines outcomes. We instead model effort as an allocation across methods with heterogeneous effectiveness. Combining panel surveys, administrative records, digital activity logs, and a randomized information intervention with over 2,000 undergraduates, we test whether imperfect information leads to effort misallocation and quantify consequences for performance. At baseline, students hold divergent beliefs, and many devote time to passive strategies such as rereading, despite evidence that active retrieval is more effective; these choices predict lower performance and larger self-assessment errors. We randomize treated students into general-feedback and personalized-feedback arms, benchmarking habits against peers in the latter. General feedback has little effect. Personalized feedback widens the perceived effectiveness gap between active and passive methods by 42 percent, shifts time toward effective practices, and raises exam scores by 0.05–0.08 standard deviations. A dynamic model with learning-by-doing and convex allocation costs shows that, for students with the weakest baseline beliefs, personalized feedback is equivalent to a 16.5 percent reduction in adoption costs. These results identify information frictions about multidimensional effort as a determinant of academic performance.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Forecasting the Covid Surge in Inflation
affiliations: Princeton University - Princeton School of Public and International Affairs

detail.title: Forecasting the Covid Surge in Inflation
detail.abstract:
The persistent surge in U.S. inflation that began in 2021 caught forecasters and policymakers by surprise. The 2021 inflation shocks were viewed as transitory, not persistent, leading to large forecast errors in late 2021 and 2022. This paper asks whether time series models – using only data on current and past inflation, but incorporating stochastic volatility and exhibiting time-varying persistence – performed better. Univariate models, using real-time data, did not. Multivariate models, incorporating sectoral inflation measures, did.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Heterogeneous Globalization: Offshoring and Reorganization
affiliations: Dartmouth College, Dartmouth College - Tuck School of Business, Aarhus University and

detail.title: Heterogeneous Globalization: Offshoring and Reorganization
detail.abstract: This paper uses a unique offshoring survey to show that firms import the same goods they manufacture at home after they relocate production to low-wage countries. Instead of ceasing domestic production, offshorers produce higher-priced domestic varieties and increase both the shares and levels of their employment in innovation-related occupations. These responses highlight an under-explored aspect of globalization: the opportunity to offshore production of low-end varieties and focus domestic activities on the development, production, and marketing of high-quality or technologically advanced versions.

title: Does Mining Centralization Matter? Experimental Evidence from Automated Market Makers

detail.title: Does Mining Centralization Matter? Experimental Evidence from Automated Market Makers
detail.abstract: We study whether mining centralization affects price formation in cryptocurrency markets. Theory offers opposing predictions: concentration may enable strategic supply behavior, yet pooling may simply redistribute risk. We address this question using a laboratory experiment that embeds mining into an automated market maker (AMM) trading environment. Comparing solo and pooled mining, we find that centralization has no effect on price levels or volatility when pooling functions as a pure risk-sharing mechanism. This neutrality holds across distinct valuation environments. At the same time, we document systematic price declines in our environment, driven by continued asset issuance under a fixed participant base. We further show that exogenous demand shocks increase prices and trading activity but do not generate persistent distortions. In addition, we show that mining centralization affects the traders on an individual level by reducing the frequency of suboptimal trading behavior. Our results reconcile conflicting theoretical predictions and demonstrate that market microstructure, specifically AMMs, plays a central role in determining whether mining centralization matters for price formation.

title: Policy Thresholds as Growth Barriers: Theory and Evidence from a Payroll Tax Notch
affiliations: Labour Institute for Economic Research, University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB) - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Policy Thresholds as Growth Barriers: Theory and Evidence from a Payroll Tax Notch
detail.abstract: Discrete policy thresholds are pervasive in tax and regulatory systems and can substantially distort behavior. We show that notches acting as barriers to mobility within a distribution generate distortions extending far beyond the threshold. The same mechanism biases conventional difference-in-differences estimators, and we propose a new methodology to recover causal effects. Applying the method to the abolition of a size-based payroll tax notch, we find that the notch reduced the number of firms above the threshold by 18 percent and lowered treated firms' employment, capital stock, and value added by 10 percent, whereas conventional difference-in-differences estimates imply negligible effects.

title: Eigenmanifold in Game: Evidence from Human Continuous Strategy Game Experiments
